name: Jade Emperor Pagoda
kicker: Three halls at 73 Mai Thị Lựu
summary: The Jade Emperor Pagoda is the temple hour that is not the cathedral. Visit HCMC says it was built about 1892–1900 by Lưu Minh, from Guangdong, and renamed Phước Hải Tự in 1984. The compound is 2,300 m², with about 300 wooden statues. Visit HCMC prints 7:00–17:30 every day, and 5:00–19:00 on the 1st and 15th of the lunar month. A fee was not printed.
fee: Check on arrival. No fee was printed.
getThere: Buses 18, 93, and 150, then a walk. Mai Thị Lựu is narrow.

notice.title: Ask before you photograph inside
notice.body: Visit HCMC says to ask before photographing inside. The second photograph is an altar. It is not a substitute for that ask.

body: The address is 73 Mai Thị Lựu. Visit HCMC says Tan Dinh Ward, District 1, and notes the ward wording as updated. The 1994 ranking is a national architectural and artistic monument. Other names are Điện Ngọc Hoàng and Phước Hải Tự. Visit HCMC says Lưu Minh, dharma name Lưu Đạo Nguyên, built it, and that Thích Vĩnh Khương brought it into the Vietnam Buddhist Sangha in 1982.

Three halls. Front: door gods, the earth god, the tiger general. Center: the Jade Emperor, Nam Tào, Bắc Đẩu, the Medicine Buddha, Chuẩn Đề, Huyền Thiên Đại Đế. Rear: the ten kings of hell, the matchmakers, Kim Hoa Thánh Mẫu, Quan Âm. It is not Giác Lâm. That pagoda is a different ward and a different century. Weekday or early morning is the page’s advice. The photograph is the gate and the board, not a coil of incense.

gettingThere: Visit HCMC names buses 18, 93, and 150 to Điện Biên Phủ, Đinh Tiên Hoàng, or Nguyễn Đình Chiểu, then a walk. From here Visit HCMC prints about 3.1 km to the opera, 2.6 km to the post office, 2.5 km to the cathedral, and 2.7 km to the palace. Check on arrival.
